chunk_findings.detail: The new helper does not canonicalize the result of `G.family_name_of(...)` before it is compared with the lower-cased family produced by the fallback path. The conflict check therefore depends on the exact spelling stored in `[agent].families` / `[agent].family`. For example, with `[agent].families = ["DeepSeek"]`, `[agent].family = "DeepSeek"`, and reviewer `--model deepseek-chat`, `_family_of_name_or_value(model, cfg)` returns `"deepseek"` via `G.family_of(...).strip().lower()`, while `_family_of_name_or_value(author, cfg)` returns `"DeepSeek"` via `G.family_name_of(...)`. The comparison fails, the function returns `""`, and a same-family reviewer gate is not refused even though the old code always lower-cased both sides.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:_family_of_name_or_value

chunk_findings.detail: The function returns the lower-cased model string rather than the configured family value. For example, with a legal configuration `families = {"qwen": "Alibaba"}`, `family_name_of("Alibaba", families)` returns `"alibaba"`, which is not one of `families.values()` and not the family name the configuration actually uses. If `complete` stores this as the event’s `author_family` while reviewer-family lookup (`family_of`) returns the configured `"Alibaba"`, a case-sensitive same-family comparison will treat an Alibaba author and Alibaba reviewer as different, allowing a same-family review to pass. The comparison may be case-insensitive, but the returned/stored identity should be canonical (or both sides must be normalized consistently), not an arbitrary lower-cased copy of the input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/agent.py:family_name_of

chunk_findings.detail: The reviewer-side family resolution is not case-normalised when the family comes from `family_name_of`. The helper computes `fam = _declared_family(rec.evidence) or family_name_of(m, cfg.agent.families) or family_of(m, cfg).strip().lower()`, so `.strip().lower()` applies only to the `family_of` fallback, while the author-side expression lower-cases the whole `family_name_of(...) or family_of(...)` result. Given a configured family name such as `cfg.agent.families = {"DeepSeek": ...}` and a reviewer gate whose evidence model is the bare family name `"DeepSeek"`, `_reviewer_fams` stores `fam == "DeepSeek"` while `author_fam` for the same family is `"deepseek"`. The later exact comparison therefore treats the reviewer as a different family, allowing a same-family reviewer to pass the independence gate (or allowing two same-family reviewers to be counted as distinct), contrary to the comment that family comparison is case-blind.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:_reviewer_fams

chunk_findings.detail: `test_gate_record_refuses_the_configured_family_without_a_session_model` can pass without exercising the configured author-family path. It ignores the return value of `write_config` at line 126, so a failed config write (for example, a schema or key error) would not be detected. It then only asserts that stderr contains `--reviewer-model` at line 133; it never asserts that the refusal mentions `deepseek`, the configured family, or a same-family/author-family reason. If the CLI refuses `--model deepseek` for an unrelated reason—such as a generic “reviewer model required” or usage error that happens to mention `--reviewer-model`—the test still passes even though the new `[agent].family` reading logic was never used.
